name: Fort Lytton
scope: Whole surviving Fort Lytton: actual pentagonal main earthworks/open grassy court/moat/causeway and entry passage, northern and northwestern casemates with seven gun positions and defining restored artillery, engine-room/coal-store corner, two mapped southern/eastern brick stores and surviving concrete slabs. Western battery/pits5and6, WWII searchlight and command-post remnants, bounded gun-cotton-store/priming-pit ruins and1903 searchlight/old jetty/winch-block traces where primary relative information supports them. Neighbouring Lytton Quarantine Station/chimney/refinery, museum display collections unrelated to fixed positions, modern shelters/movie-set remnants/picnic equipment/boats/trees/people/inscriptions excluded.
era: Surviving heritage fort and fixed artillery reconstruction, using current primary QHR600248 description (2024 revisions), native OSM detailed plans and exact2010 creator-PD photographs. Fine current repairs, unseen sections, unmapped western traces and grading are explicit estimates.

references.caption: Armstrong BL 6-inch Mk V disappearing gun (hydraulically controlled) at Fort Lytton, Brisbane, Australia.

originalReview.notes: Exact3888x2592 original individually inspected: restored six-inch Armstrong disappearing mounting inside circular concrete/brick pit, white/gray barrel with open muzzle/breech and black mechanical yoke/circular platform/cross arms, slender vertical supports and sheet-metal protective cover overhead. Real arched passage behind; painted labels/museum signage not copied. Mechanical dimensions are bounded medium-fi approximations, not engineering reconstruction.

references.caption:
Gun aimed at river, Fort Lytton, Brisbane, Australia. Appears to be the remains of QF 4.7 inch gun installed in World War II, in gun pit number 4, to guard the boom defences.
Comment : See File:4.7 inch gun and crew Fort Lytton 1943 AWM 060050.jpeg for what apperas to be the same gun with its crew in 1943.

originalReview.notes: Exact3888x2592 original individually inspected: gun-pit4 concrete curved overhead protection with open sides and genuine tall rear slots/low opening; long pale naval-gun barrel elevated riverward, open muzzle and gray mounting/shield. Concrete formwork/weathering is visible. Background quarantine structures/people/signage not included; no copied weathering texture.

references.caption: Gun-cotton store at Fort Lytton, Brisbane, Australia. Made in 1884, used for ammunition from 1908.

originalReview.notes: Exact3888x2592 original individually inspected: open roofless brick gun-cotton-store excavation, low irregular surviving brick walls/whitewashed lower lining, rectangular divided bays and a central floor drain. No intact roof or reconstructed complete building is claimed. Unmapped exact store/priming-pit location is bounded by primary relative text across the moat from the engine room; exact rubble census/hidden sides estimated.

externalReferences.caption: Inside the moat of Fort Lytton, Brisbane, Australia.

originalReview.notes: Exact3489x2315 original individually inspected: current inner court, rough whitewashed/concrete casemate fronts, true arched openings, rectangular recesses and open stairs rising to turfed banks. High right northern casemate has recessed tall slit/doorway census, short red corrugated loading-gallery awning, flat copings. Near-left northwest arc shows low gun-pit access fronts and grassy cover. It does not establish all sides or surveyed heights. People, rope barriers, labels and the neighbouring quarantine buildings are excluded.

review.method: Four exact cleared published Qualla creator-PD native originals, current primary text and actual detailed fort geometry
review.notes: Qualla-first44 source families/no metadata conflicts. Six exact local Commander Keane2010 native originals individually inspected, with matching native SHA1/revision/dimensions and own/PD-self release. Four useful originals selected (inside-court local metadata lacks an explicit PD basis, so exact unchanged Qualla bytes are copied into the model and bound to the native photographer own/PD-self grant via the existing supplemental adapter, without modifying source media): inner fort, disappearing gun, gun-pit4 naval gun, gun-cotton-store ruin. Chimney photograph depicts separate quarantine boiler precinct; Bulwer view depicts opposite-river industry, both unadopted. Licensed modern bridge/moat/museum/fortification images unused/unviewed; old people/ships/camp images unnecessary/unadopted. No supplemental imagery, generated bitmap/borrowed mesh or source-media repair. Official current primary architectural text used without gallery pixels. Parks page direct request403 was not bypassed; current heritage public data worked.
